description: SENDS a prepared post, or schedules it. THIS IS IRREVERSIBLE: the post goes out under the user's own name and nothing here can take it down. ASK THE USER FIRST, IN THE SAME MESSAGE THAT NAMES WHAT WILL GO OUT: the account, the text, the visibility, and the time if it is scheduled. Wait for their explicit go. A bare 'yes' only counts if your ask for THIS post was the message immediately before it. IF THE PUBLISH CARD ALREADY TOOK THEIR APPROVAL, that message IS the go and it names the post id to use: call this with that id and nothing else (do not prepare again; this tool takes no caption, visibility or disclosure: what they set in the card is what goes out). THE ONE THING YOU CAN STILL CHANGE IS THE TIME: `schedule_at` here overrides whatever the card staged, so passing it (or null, to send a scheduled post now) publishes at a time the person did not approve: leave it alone unless they asked you to, in this conversation, since they confirmed. WHEN: after `prepare_post`, once the user has chosen and confirmed. IT NEVER ANSWERS `posted`, and that is the truth, not a delay: TikTok answers `publishing` (the platform downloads the video itself, which can still fail); YouTube and Instagram answer `submitted` (aicut's poster has it, nothing is confirmed); a scheduled post answers `scheduled`. Poll `get_post_status` until `posted` or `failed`; never tell the user their video is live on the strength of this call. SCHEDULING: `schedule_at` sets or moves the time, null sends a post prepared for later now. A scheduled TikTok or Instagram post waits in aicut (the scheduler fires every due post at once, so a schedule can be REFUSED with `retry_after_seconds` meaning 'move it at least this many seconds later'); a scheduled YouTube post is uploaded at once as private and published by YouTube, so it stays `scheduled` with a `post_id` you can hand the user. THE POSTING LIMITS, so you can pace a batch instead of discovering them: per CONNECTED ACCOUNT, tiktok 5/min and 13/24h, youtube 2/min and 10/24h, instagram 4/min and 25/24h. Both windows are ROLLING (the 24h one does not reset at midnight). Over the limit you get a 429 (`post_rate_limited` or `daily_post_limit`) with `retry_after_seconds`: respect it, and do not prepare a second post or use a second account to get around it. A slot is taken only by a call that reaches the platform, so every refusal raised before that point is FREE (a 400, 404, 409 `already_published` / `post_expired` / `consent_required` / `video_not_ready`, a 403 `insufficient_scope`, a TikTok preflight failure): fix it and retry at once. `prepare_post` is a separate meter (5/min, 100/24h per connected account). Scheduling spends the same allowance, counted around the scheduled time. 403 `insufficient_scope` = the user's connection lacks the `social:publish` permission: not a bad `video_id` or `account_id`, and a retry cannot fix it. Tell them to disconnect and reconnect aicut at https://www.aicut.pro/account/settings#connections (the full steps are in `prepare_post`'s REFUSALS), then STOP. A 403 here posted NOTHING: the request never reached the platform, so say plainly that the video did not go out.

schedule_at.description: ISO-8601 time to publish at, at least 10 minutes ahead; overrides what `prepare_post` recorded. Null sends the post now. Omit to keep the prepared time.

name: publish_post
title: Publish a prepared post
